newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end firm to higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end firm to higher.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond cash prices ended firm to slightly higher but lagged muni futures Tuesday as a big Texas note deal priced and roughly $400 million of bid lists hit the Street.

"Constant customer selling" beset Tuesday's "very frustrating" session as customers appeared to be lightening up ahead of what could be a building calendar, the trader said. Bond funds accounted for most of the lists, he said.
"The calendar again is going to be a concern," the trader said. "Coming not this week but the following week I think it starts to build," the trader said.
Standard & Poor's Blue List of dealer inventory remains in the $1.4 billion range, though it dropped to $1.432 billion Tuesday from $1.467 billion on Monday.

"That just means that dealers such as ourselves are long bonds, maybe some dealers are longer than others," the trader said, adding that market has been volatile of late. A stronger-than-expected July durable goods report triggered a sharp bond market sell off on Friday, and continued to exert pressure on Monday.
"People are a little skittish in here," a trader said.
Cash is scarce and customers are selective, the trader said, adding that the new issue market will be "the marquee part of the market."
"People are just looking for that to be priced to sell, they are looking for their bargains there," he said.

A municipal analyst said high-grade issues improved by two basis points overall Tuesday, while dollar bonds ended flat to slightly better. Activity was light to moderate. Local and regional competitive issues were firmly bid.
In debt futures, the September municipal contract closed up 24/32 at 114-17/32.
The September T-bond contract closed up 10/32 at 108-30/32. The MOB spread was 179 ticks.
"Today we had a little firmness on the contract which gave some ray of hope," one muni trader said. While cash failed to follow suit on Tuesday, that could change Wednesday, he said.

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond closed up 10/32 at 97-6/32 to yield 6.97 percent. Treasuries opened higher Tuesday helped by overseas buying. They later surrendered some ground after the Conference Board said consumer confidence rose to a new six-year high of 109.4 in August from a revised reading of 107.0 in July.
Turning to the short-term municipal market, 16 firms won portions of Texas' $2.9 billion tax and revenue anticipation note offering. The aggregate net interest cost was 3.99619755921 percent.
"It was a good one," John Bell, assistant deputy Treasurer for the Texas State Treasury said. "Everybody who bid won a portion of it."

The offering drew 72 separate bids totaling nearly $10 billion from 16 different syndicates, Bell said. The NIC on last year's Texas TRANs deal, which totaled some $2.4 billion, was about 4.11 percent, he said.
"We're just happy with it, and everything has worked out, and we close on (August) 30, this Friday," Bell said.

Looking ahead, Wednesday's scheduled negotiated sales are expected to number 14 and total $781 million. Topping the list is a $377 million New York State Dormitory Authority offering via Smith Barney Inc.
Just six competitive sales totaling $31 million are expected. The largest is an $11.4 million Avalon, N.J., deal set for 1100 EDT.
--Kathie O'Donnell, 212-859-1655
